article.title: Vermont Socialist: November 2026
article.author: Green Mountain DSA
article.content: HELP SHAPE OUR NEXT YEAR: ANNUAL CONVENTION, SUNDAY, NOVEMBER 15 Green Mountain DSA’s annual convention is Sunday, November 15, at the Socialist Labor Party Hall, 46 Granite Street in Barre. We’ll begin around 11 a.m. and continue through the late afternoon. At convention, we’ll elect chapter officers and committee chairs and consider resolutions and bylaws amendments that will shape our work in the coming year. We strongly encourage members to attend in person. It’s a chance to meet comrades from across Vermont and have a say in what we take on together. A virtual option is also available. Register in advance and find convention details. The convention page also has the form for nominating chapter officers and committee chairs. FIVE GREEN MOUNTAIN DSA ENDORSEES HEADED TO MONTPELIER AND A BIG NIGHT FOR DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS NATIONWIDE While we’re disappointed that Phil Scott won a sixth term as governor, Tuesday was a night where working people made it clear that it's time for change here in Vermont and nationwide. Working Vermonters still need housing we can afford, healthcare we can count on, and public services that meet our needs. We’ll keep organizing for those priorities in our communities and at the State House. We’re proud to celebrate five of our six endorsed candidates winning seats in the Vermont General Assembly. Tanya Vyhovsky won reelection to the Vermont Senate, and Trang Do, Jeffrey Peterson, Matt Gile, and Adam Franz won seats in the Vermont House. We also thank Alexander Bobella and the volunteers who worked on his Senate campaign laying the groundwork for a socialist flip in that county in the future. Thank you to everyone who knocked doors, talked to neighbors, and helped get out the vote. When the legislature convenes, those same relationships will matter as we organize around the issues we heard about on the doorstep. Across the country, voters delivered a blow to the Trump administration by taking both chambers of Congress out of Republican hands. DSA candidates also won races for Congress, state legislatures, and local office. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Rashida Tlaib won reelection to the U.S. House. They’ll be joined by Darializa Avila Chevalier, Claire Valdez, Donavan McKinney, Melat Kiros, Chris Rabb, and Angela Gonzales-Torres. These wins give working people more allies in office as we organize for universal healthcare, stronger labor rights, and an end to ICE. See DSA’s nationwide election results . TAX THE RICH: MONTPELIER AND WINOOSKI CANVASSES FOR TOWN MEETING DAY 2027 BALLOT QUESTIONS Our Tax the Rich campaign is calling on Vermont lawmakers to raise taxes on the richest 5 percent, tax the proceeds of wealth, and use the revenue to make healthcare affordable and accessible. In Montpelier and Winooski, the campaign has been working to put advisory questions on the Town Meeting Day 2027 ballots so residents can weigh in. Sign up to help us collect signatures on our Tax the Rich ballot petitions (advisory questions for the Town Meeting Day Ballot in Montpelier and Winooski)! Winooski -- Saturday, November 14, 1-3 p.m. @ 53 Lafountain St. Montpelier -- Sunday, November 22, 10 a.m. to 12 p.m. @ Montpelier High School Winooski -- Sunday, November 29, 1-3 p.m. @ 53 Lafountain St. Sign up GREEN MOUNTAIN DSA MONTH IN REVIEW In the final weeks before Election Day, members knocked doors for our endorsed candidates, including Adam Franz in Burlington and Alexander Bobella in Franklin County. Thank you to everyone who spent part of an October evening or weekend out talking with neighbors. On October 26, members joined the May Day Strong coalition at Burlington City Hall to oppose the Burlington Forward resolution and its push for more policing. Earlier in the month, we stood with UVM Staff United at its October 20 bargaining kickoff outside Howe Library. University staff are fighting for a fair contract, and we were glad to show that their fight has support beyond campus. Members also worked with comrades in Southern Vermont to build a local presence, including a general interest meeting in Brattleboro, and prepared proposals for our November convention. We closed out the month with a group outing to The Rocky Horror Picture Show . After weeks of canvassing and meetings, it was good to spend an evening together at the movies. WE’RE BUILDING A FAMILY-FRIENDLY GMDSA Green Mountain Democratic Socialists of America is working towards making our organization more accessible to parents and guardians. In August we were approved to receive a chapter Growth and Development grant from DSA national to help with this effort, among other priorities. You can help us by letting us know if you would benefit from childcare being offered at our general meetings. Please fill out our Childcare Needs Survey: https://forms.gle/6Mq1KHWGrc3QgLGv8 UPCOMING GREEN MOUNTAIN DSA MEETINGS Our Labor Committee meets on the second Monday of every month at 6:00pm on Zoom , including Monday Nov 09 . Talk about your job and learn about shop-floor organizing from peers at Workers' Circle (co-hosted with the Green Mountain IWW) on the second and fourth Wednesdays of each month, including Wednesday Nov 11 at 6:00pm at Migrant Justice (179 S. Winooski Ave in Burlington). Our annual chapter convention is Sunday Nov 15 at the Socialist Labor Party Hall (46 Granite St in Barre). This is the most important GMDSA event of the year! The convention will open promptly at 11:00am. Members: check your DSA email for further communication about submitting bylaws amendments and resolutions for debate at convention and to register. Add our Google Calendar - Check out our website - Follow us on Instagram , Threads , Facebook , and BlueSky IMPORTANT DATES THIS YEAR Wednesday, November 11, 6 p.m. ET | Workers’ Circle. Join Green Mountain DSA and the Green Mountain IWW at Migrant Justice, 179 South Winooski Avenue in Burlington, to talk with other workers about organizing on the job. Sunday, November 15, around 11 a.m. ET | Annual convention. Register and find event details. Saturday, November 21, 10 am - 12 pm.
